title: Contract deviation sandbox to simulate pricing exposure and auto-approve rules
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a lightweight 'contract deviation sandbox' that lets Sales/Legal/PM simulate the downstream pricing and indemnity exposure of proposed MSA/DPA concessions and test auto-approve thresholds. The sandbox should: 1) Accept a structured set of clause deltas (liability cap, indemnity carveouts, data residency exceptions, escrow requests). 2) Run a pricing impact simulation using historical contract telemetry and pricing rules. 3) Output a recommended approval action (auto-approve, require manager + legal, escalate to CRO) and a human-readable rationale. Purpose: accelerate small concession approvals for PLG/SMB deals while surfacing high-risk deviations for fulsome review.
acceptance_criteria: Sandbox accepts JSON/plaintext clause deltas and maps them to canonical deviation types
Pricing simulator returns quantitative estimate of ARR / margin impact and highlights assumptions
Decision engine flags auto-approve when deviation score < 25 and no security flags
Legal can add rule overrides and annotate rationales in the output
UI/CSV export for sales enablement and audit trails
Telemetry captured to track auto-approve accuracy vs. post-signature incidents
steps: Kickoff with Legal, Sales Ops, and Pricing (done 2025-02-18)
Create schema of common concession types and canonical mapping (owner: Marco)
Prototype a ruleset-driven decision engine using past contract dataset (owner: Data Team)
Implement lightweight web UI for clause input and simulation results (owner: Growth Eng)
Run shadow mode pilot on 100 historical redlines to validate false positive rate
Iterate rules for indemnity/liability caps and integrate security flags
Enable opt-in auto-approve for SMB segment with 2-week monitoring window
Formalize audit log export and update contract intake SOPs
comments: 2025-02-18 Asha: Kickoff complete. Legal outlined three high-risk deviation buckets we must always escalate (data residency, criminal-indemnity carveouts, escrow with source access). Sales Ops asked for CSV export to plug into quoting tool.
2025-02-21 Marco: Drafted canonical mapping of 18 deviation types and scoring weights. Shared with pricing for initial rule coefficients.
2025-02-25 Priya (Legal): Reviewed mapping; asked to add a 'Regulated Data' binary flag and require security review for >$250k ARR deals. Marked security_review_required true for the pilot.

2025-02-28 Data Team: Completed historical run of 320 redlines. Preliminary model estimates that 64% of small deviations would have been safe for auto-approve at current pricing rules; false positive projection ~6% (need validation).
2025-03-03 Growth Eng: Prototype UI up at /sandbox (internal only). It displays deviation score, pricing delta, and recommended action. Still missing Legal override flow.

2025-03-05 Asha: Decided to run a 30-day shadow pilot (no auto-approves) on new inbound redlines for SMB accounts to measure precision. If precision > 92% and no missed security flags, enable opt-in auto-approve for SMBs.
notes: Trade-offs: a rules-first approach is fast to ship but will need periodic tuning. Consider ML classifier in Q3 if shadow-mode data supports it.
We must surface explainability for any auto-approve decision to satisfy Legal and Sales auditors (audit trail requirement).
Plan to add a 'manual quick-approve' button backed by templated guardrails for AE Managers in V1.
